12-feat-render-a-stack-overview-block-in.description: #12: feat: render a stack overview block in each PR description

context.text: sr implement --sandbox crashed ('.worktrees/<b> already exists') when run from inside a worktree. Worktree location was computed from 3 places using 2 anchors: WorktreeAdd + implement.go JSON used c.Git.Dir (current checkout); sandbox used mainRoot (parent of git-common-dir). They diverge from any worktree, so scaffold created the worktree at one path and SandboxRun's dirExists guard checked the other, missed it, and re-created -> collision.

Unified all worktree-path computation on the MAIN repo root via a single worktreesRoot(c) helper (sandbox.MainRoot(absGitCommonDir(c))/.worktrees). WorktreeAdd/Remove now pass absolute main-root paths; implement.go reports the same; ensureGitExclude writes to the shared .git/info/exclude. Fixes the crash and makes --sandbox workdir correct from any checkout.

skill-prompt-block.description: sr claude install injects an always-on stackr pointer block into CLAUDE.md (managed, idempotent, reversible, --no-prompt-block opt-out)

context.text: sr claude install injects a marker-delimited stackr pointer block into CLAUDE.md (always-on), closing the gap where the skill's description might not trigger before an agent reaches for raw git

Prompt content lives in .claude/prompts/stackr.md (single source of truth); CLAUDE.md imports it via marker-delimited @.claude/prompts/stackr.md. --local targets cwd's .claude (root pre-run exempts claude --local so it works outside a repo). Content adds sr up/down navigation + stack-sequential-work blurb.

skill-redesign.description: Reexamine and possibly unify the Claude Code skills (stackr, sr-sandbox, sr-implement) from first principles

context.text: Unified the 3 Claude skills (stackr/sr-sandbox/sr-implement) into ONE skill at .claude/skills/stackr/ with progressive disclosure: SKILL.md + sandbox.md + implement.md
Cross-skill refs aren't load-bearing (skills load independently); same-dir progressive disclosure IS reliable. One description routes all 3 intents. Kills 3-way drift + mechanism split.
Stayed with skill over MCP per ADR-0003 (MCP built+removed; CLI already emits JSON via --aiprepare; ~50 tools = permanent context tax)
Defer command flags to 'sr --help' (drift-proof); keep only compact command MAP inline so agents can discover commands they'd otherwise never --help
Consider an ADR for the unified-skill + go:embed-dir + drift-test pattern if it proves durable
